_comment.about: corporate/corporate/nextjs is the Next.js half of corporate_sdk, the company pages: in 1.0.0 the LEGAL pages only. Ray, 2026-09-10: "supa has no terms pages or about page"; asked where they belong, "legal pages are not in corporate sdk?" and "you should look at the dart side if they are not there yet" - on the Dart side corporate/corporate/dart (corporate_sdk 1.2.0) owns TermPage / PolicyPage at /term and /policy and every composition with auth_sdk includes it, so this half mirrors that ownership: it installs app/legal/page.tsx (the index of the shell's published legal documents) and app/legal/[id]/page.tsx (one document; 404 when missing or disabled), both server components with no "use client" (the first HTML carries the words; generateMetadata takes the document's title through base_sdk's buildPageMetadata), the renderer components/custom/legal/legal-doc.tsx (LegalDoc, normaliseLegalDoc, LegalDocView: title + the body as text with whitespace kept at prose width - the way rokct.ai's hand-rolled app/legal/[id]/page.tsx renders it), the frame components/custom/legal/legal-frame.tsx (the host's PLATFORM_NAME linking home, the content, and base_sdk's FooterChromeRow carrying the Legal link group built from the same documents), the guest read app/actions/corporate/legal.ts getPublicTerm(name) (frappe.client.get on doctype "Terms and Conditions" through base_sdk's platform gateway with no credentials, mirroring rokct.ai's TermsService.getSystemTerm; null with no backend) and the ONE seam the pages read through, components/custom/legal/load-legal-doc.ts: loadLegalDoc(slug) and loadLegalIndex(). The list comes from base_sdk >= 1.37.0's app/actions/base/legal.ts listPublicTerms() and the links from its components/custom/landing/legal-links.ts (legalFooterLinks, legalDocHref, LEGAL_DOCTYPE, LEGAL_ROUTE), so the footer row these pages draw is the row a home SDK's footer draws once it passes FooterChromeConfig.links - base carries the links and the read, this SDK the pages. Composed into every Next.js shell with auth (hosting, supacharge, rokctapp templates in the-rokct-protocol core/utils/frappe/composer), never as the home SDK (home_sdk false). Ray, 2026-09-10 22:14Z: corporate_sdk owns the company pages (legal, about, team) as renderers, with content from the shell's data/ folder on local / hybrid shells - base 1.35.0 adds that server-only reader, and corporate_sdk 1.1.0 adds the about / team pages and the data/ fallback inside loadLegalDoc / loadLegalIndex without touching the pages. No dependencies of its own (react, next and base's installs), no integrations: the routes are file-convention pages. tests/test_manifest.py holds the installs, the floors, that every entry module is directive-free, that the document page 404s a missing or disabled document, and that nothing rendered carries placeholder words.
_comment.app/actions/base/legal.ts: installed by base_sdk >= 1.37.0 (listPublicTerms(), the guest read of every enabled "Terms and Conditions" document that loadLegalIndex() and the footer's Legal row are built from)
_comment.app/config/platform.ts: host shell (PLATFORM_NAME, the name the legal frame's home link shows; never written here)
_comment.app/lib/site-metadata.ts: installed by base_sdk >= 1.20.0 (buildPageMetadata, the page-scope metadata builder generateMetadata hands the document's title to)
_comment.app/services/base/platform-gateway.ts: installed by base_sdk >= 1.3.0 (platformCall with requireAuth false, the guest gateway read getPublicTerm makes)
_comment.components/custom/footer-chrome.tsx: installed by base_sdk >= 1.37.0 (FooterChromeRow drawing FooterChromeConfig.links; before 1.37.0 the row takes no links and the legal frame's group is a type error)
_comment.components/custom/landing/footer-chrome-: installed by base_sdk >= 1.37.0 (FooterChromeConfig.links, FooterLinkGroup; FOOTER_CHROME_CONFIG the frame extends)
_comment.components/custom/landing/legal-links.ts: installed by base_sdk >= 1.37.0 (LEGAL_DOCTYPE, LEGAL_ROUTE, DEFAULT_LEGAL_GROUP_LABEL, PublicTerm, legalDocHref, legalFooterLinks - the pure half the pages and the frame share with the footer)
